content.title: Charles Schwab to acquire Forge in $660M deal: CEO explains why
content.description:
Charles Schwab (SCHW) CEO Rick Wurster joins Market Catalysts with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss the company's acquisition of Forge (FRGE) and to explain why Charles Schwab is expanding its private market offerings for investors.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Catalysts.

content.title: Schwab notches a $660 million deal agreement with private asset firm Forge Global Holdings
content.summary: Charles Schwab said Thursday that it's buying publicly traded investing platform Forge Global Holdings, which acts as a marketplace for pre-IPO companies, for $660 million.

content.title: Charles Schwab Wants to Provide Clients With Access to Private Assets. It’s Buying Forge Global.
content.summary: The deal would enable Schwab to offer individual investors and financial advisors greater access to private markets at a time when more companies are electing to remain private.

content.title: Charles Schwab to Allow Investments in Private Companies, Joining a Wall Street Craze
content.summary: Charles Schwab  is the latest Wall Street firm to take a big step into the world of private markets.  The brokerage firm that pioneered discount stock-trading for individual investors agreed to buy  Forge Global  one of the major platforms that allows investors to buy shares in promising private companies.  Forge Global is a marketplace where investors can buy a stake in late-stage startups like crypto exchange Kraken and artificial-intelligence leader OpenAI.

content.title: Schwab RIA Member Program to Launch with 10 Firms in 2026
content.summary: Schwab expects to add roughly 10 RIAs a month, with services including business and growth consulting, advisor coaching and curated products from third-party vendors with potential discounts.

content.title: Schwab Agrees to Buy Private Share Platform for $660M
content.summary: The deal is the first under CEO Rick Wurster, and would give customers more opportunities to gain exposure to unlisted companies.

content.summary: HOOD's third-quarter 2025 profit and revenues soar on robust trading and NIR growth, yet the stock dips as expenses climb.

content.title: Schwab CEO: Financial Services Need to Beef Up Convenience
content.summary: In his first address as CEO of Schwab at Impact, Rick Wurster told RIAs that advisors need to catch up with the “bull market for convenience” to retain and attract clients.
